relatedEntities.notes: Site-specific impurity profile — validate against method

properties.solubility: Practically insoluble in water; soluble in organic solvents

hazardStatements: Review current SDS for solid API and intermediates
hazards.notes: Route-specific hazards are dominated by HF (BHC), flammable solvents, and catalytic hydrogenation where used. Always map intermediate SDS packages.

overview: Ibuprofen manufacture is a flagship example of industrial process chemistry evolution. The Boots classical route (six steps) was largely superseded by the BHC (Hoechst-Celanese) process: catalytic carbonylation of 1-(4-isobutylphenyl)ethanol, offering higher atom economy and fewer steps. This dossier emphasizes the BHC-style industrial logic and plant implications.
manufacturingSummary: Modern plants favor short catalytic routes (BHC-type) with HF or alternative carbonylation systems, careful materials of construction for HF service, and crystallization of the racemic acid. Chirality is typically not resolved for classic racemic ibuprofen API.

environmentBaseline.atmosphere: Inerting for catalytic and HF service as required
environmentBaseline.containment: HF service requires specialized containment, detection, and emergency response
environmentBaseline.atexZone: Solvent handling areas classified per site assessment
environmentBaseline.notes: HF metallurgy and elastomer compatibility are design-critical; many facilities use dedicated HF units.

ehsHighlights: Anhydrous HF: extreme hazard — dedicated design, PPE, calcium gluconate readiness

apparatusCatalog.notes: If upstream ketone hydrogenation is on-site

routes.name: BHC-type catalytic carbonylation (modern industrial)
routes.summary: 1-(4-Isobutylphenyl)ethanol undergoes acid-catalyzed carbonylation (classically anhydrous HF / CO with Pd catalyst systems in published descriptions) to ibuprofen with high atom economy. Exact catalyst packages are proprietary; use patents for freedom-to-operate analysis.
advantages: Fewer steps vs classical Boots route
Industry benchmark for green process redesign
disadvantages: HF or equivalent superacid systems demand specialist plant design

materials.name: 1-(4-Isobutylphenyl)ethanol (IBPE)
materials.notes: Often from hydrogenation of corresponding ketone

materials.name: Anhydrous hydrogen fluoride (classical BHC medium)
materials.notes: Extreme hazard; alternatives exist in literature/patents

steps.title: Upstream IBPE supply (ketone hydrogenation)
steps.description: If integrated, hydrogenate 4-isobutylacetophenone to 1-(4-isobutylphenyl)ethanol over a suitable metal catalyst. Control over-reduction and isomer impurities.
steps.mechanismNotes: Heterogeneous hydrogenation delivers the benzylic alcohol. Chemoselectivity vs aromatic ring reduction is managed by catalyst choice, pressure, and temperature.
steps.scaleNotes: Gas–liquid mass transfer and catalyst filtration scale non-linearly; define filtration flux at pilot.

steps.title: Carbonylation to ibuprofen
steps.description: Carbonylate IBPE in the process acid/catalyst system under CO to form the carboxylic acid. Maintain strict materials compatibility and gas handling protocols.
steps.mechanismClass: Acid-mediated carbonylation / Koch-type industrial carbonylation logic
steps.mechanismNotes: Under strong acid and CO, the benzylic system is converted to the carboxylic acid (ibuprofen). Published industrial descriptions emphasize Pd catalysis in HF media; mechanism details are package-specific. Treat as high-hazard catalytic process chemistry.
steps.scaleNotes: Never scale HF/CO chemistry without specialist process safety and metallurgy review.

steps.title: Workup, crystallization, finishing
steps.description: Quench/neutralize acid system per package, extract or crystallize ibuprofen, purify to API grade, dry and mill as required.

routes.isolation: Crystallization from process solvents; washes; vacuum dry; optional micronization for formulation.

scaleUp.labToKilo: Do not run HF chemistry in improvised lab setups. Use licensed packages and trained crews only.
scaleUp.kiloToPilot: Full process safety package: relief systems, HF detection, emergency response drills.
scaleUp.pilotToCommercial: Catalyst recycle economics; continuous or large-batch carbonylation; solvent recovery integration.
scaleUp.heatMassTransfer: CO mass transfer and multiphase mixing critical for rate and selectivity.
scaleUp.safetyScaleUp: Major accident hazard (HF, CO) — SIS, interlocks, secondary containment.
scaleUp.greenChemistryNotes: BHC route is a classic atom-economy win vs Boots; further gains via HF alternatives and catalyst turnover.

routes.name: Classical Boots multi-step route (historical)
routes.summary: Longer Friedel–Crafts / rearrangement / hydrolysis sequence historically used by Boots. Educational and legacy context; generally inferior waste profile to BHC-type routes.
advantages: Avoids HF carbonylation if that is a site constraint

steps.title: Multi-step classical sequence (summary)
steps.description: Friedel–Crafts acylation of isobutylbenzene, subsequent transformations (including Darzens or equivalent historical sequences depending on variant), and final hydrolysis to the acid. Consult detailed literature for step-by-step lab procedures—not recommended as primary commercial design.
steps.mechanismClass: Friedel–Crafts acylation + classical functional group interconversions
steps.mechanismNotes: Educational comparison route. Prefer BHC-type for green manufacturing narratives.

controls.notes: Legacy route—use only with full literature reconstruction and IP check

disclaimer: HF/CO chemistry is major-accident hazard territory. This guide is educational process intelligence only.
